reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) supports that trace O/N segregate and promote phase separation/precipitate formation (α-Ti) during 700°C aging, leading to softening, but it does not provide evidence for grain-boundary precipitation, stress concentration, brittle crack initiation, or loss of fracture toughness; the hypothesis overstates the mechanical consequences and fracture mechanism relative to the cited softening observations.
premises: Trace interstitial impurities (O, N) diffuse and segregate during high-temperature service/aging in RHEAs
Segregation induces nanoscale precipitate or intermetallic formation at grain boundaries and in the matrix
These precipitates act as stress concentrators promoting brittle crack initiation and propagation
The resulting microstructure reduces toughness and leads to brittle fracture under mechanical load
Minimizing impurity exposure during aging preserves the original toughness
